quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign like this mean?

options.text: There is roadwork ahead.
You must change lanes ahead.
There is a detour ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is roadwork ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn you about construction areas. Drive carefully.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To better see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before trying to pass them.
Because following too closely will get you caught in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: To better see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles block your view of the road ahead. Stay farther back so you can see around them and spot hazards.

questions.question: When may you legally block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered the intersection on the green light.
During rush hour traffic.
Under no circumstances.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: Never block an intersection. Even with a green light, only enter if you can cross completely before the light turns red. You can be cited for blocking.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using your high beam lights in the fog.
Staring at the road ahead of your vehicle.
Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds to stay aware. Do not stare straight ahead only. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can return to your lane when you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light at an intersection mean?

options.text: The same thing as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same thing as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: When should you not use your horn?

options.text: When visibility ahead is limited.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians. It may confuse them. Yield to them and proceed when safe.

questions.question: A yellow light turns on as you approach an intersection at the speed limit. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and proceed through the intersection without caution.
Speed up to cross the intersection before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: Yellow means the light will turn red soon. Stop safely if you can. If you cannot stop safely, cross the intersection with caution.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead is stopped to load or unload children, what must you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop until all the children have left the bus.
Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus cautiously.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
questions.explanation: Stop completely when the school bus has flashing lights and its stop arm out. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in. Make sure no children are crossing before you go.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway, if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway, if possible.
questions.explanation: Move your car completely off the road if you can. Park with all four wheels off the main part of the highway.

questions.question: It is illegal to park:

options.text: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: You cannot park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. You also cannot park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: School zone or crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or crossing.
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign warns drivers about a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous if you have a helper.
Only dangerous in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see clearly behind your vehicle. Always use extra caution when backing up.

questions.question: If your car's suspension is bad, it can cause:

options.text: Vehicle control problems.
Squealing brakes.
Slack in the steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicle control problems.
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and ride smoothly over bumps. If your vehicle bounces too much or is hard to control, your suspension may need repair.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, it is safe to return to your driving lane when:

options.text: The driver you passed signals for you to return to your lane.
You signal your intention for three seconds.
You see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Wait until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This means you have enough space to safely return to your lane.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are not easy to see; therefore, you should:

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Make constant visual checks.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make constant visual checks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss because they can hide in your blind spot. Always look carefully for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it difficult for you to see clearly, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: When visibility is poor due to darkness or bad weather, stay farther behind other vehicles. This gives you more time to stop if something unexpected happens.

questions.question: If you come to an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow light, you must:

options.text: Wait for the green light before proceeding.
Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.
Stop before crossing the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. Look for traffic and pedestrians before crossing.

questions.question: You should not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses because:

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses, due to their size and weight, require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.
Large trucks and buses travel at a higher speeds than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses, due to their size and weight, require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop than smaller cars. If you stop suddenly in front of a large vehicle, the driver may not be able to stop in time to avoid hitting you.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:

options.text: Start to prepare to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Sound a sharp blast of your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
questions.explanation: Use a sharp horn blast to warn a child or pedestrian who is about to step into the street in front of your moving vehicle.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means any driver can pass when no traffic is coming from the other direction.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. Wait until the gate is raised, you can see clearly both ways, and you are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, what should you do?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.
You must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the person is blind or partially blind. You must yield the right-of-way to these pedestrians.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings (school buses, trucks carrying hazardous materials, etc.).
Watch for multiple trains.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Be very careful at all railroad crossings. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming. Be aware that school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials must always stop at railroad crossings.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.
Stop, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on the road. You must come to a complete stop and wait until it is safe to pass through the intersection.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from the lane next to the solid yellow line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, only the traffic in the lane with the broken line can pass. Traffic in the lane with the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: A driver license can be revoked or suspended for:

options.text: Getting 12 or more points on your driving record in 12 months from traffic violations.
Changing or faking a driver license.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Your license can be revoked or suspended for faking a driver license or getting 12 or more points on your driving record in 12 months. Drivers under 18 may lose their license with just 6 points in 12 months.

questions.question: If you are in an intersection when the green light turns yellow, what should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Continue and clear the intersection safely.
Speed up so you do not cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue and clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in an intersection when the light turns yellow, move through it as quickly and safely as possible.

questions.question: As your speed increases, what is important to do?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances. When driving fast, look well ahead so you have time to react safely to hazards.

questions.question: Which vehicles are NOT required to stop before crossing a railroad grade crossing?

options.text: Farm trucks hauling produce.
School or church buses.
Taxis.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farm trucks hauling produce.
questions.explanation: School and church buses, taxis, and vehicles carrying flammable or dangerous materials must always stop at railroad crossings. Farm trucks hauling produce are not on this list.
